newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scor's Wall Street debut timed for mid-October.
newsitem.headline: Scor's Wall Street debut timed for mid-October.

text.p: Leading French reinsurer Scor SA, seeking to broaden its shareholder base, said on Monday it expected to make its debut on Wall Street in mid-October.

The announcement came as France's biggest insurer Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) said it would sell up to 30 percent of its 40.9 percent stake in Scor in an operation timed to coincide with Scor's New York listing.

Scor, following in the footsteps of French insurer Axa whose shares began trading in New York in June, said it was about to file a preliminary prospectus with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the final step before its listing.
"It should start quoting in mid-October," Scor said.
Scor, whose first-half profits rose 40 percent to 288 million francs, said merchant banks Goldman Sachs International and JP Morgan Securities would be in charge of the operation.
UAP said the sale of its Scor shares would be carried through a placement in the United States and elsewhere around the world over the next few weeks.

Scor, one of the world's 10 largest reinsurers in terms of premium income, announced in June that it planned to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange "as Wall Street was the main trading centre for reinsurance shares in the world."
At that time, UAP said it might cut its Scor holding as it no longer was a "strategic asset."

UAP said it would put some seven million shares representing 26 percent of Scor's capital up for sale. The banks in charge of the operation would have a "greenshoe" option for a further 1.05 million shares representing an additional four percent of Scor's capital to meet potential excess demand.
UAP said it was still committed to a long term relationship with Scor, which was founded in 1970 to give France a reinsurer of international standing. It will retain 10 percent of Scor.

A UAP official said the sale of the Scor shares would allow it to achieve its goal of slashing its 12 billion franc debt by half by the end of 1996. He said UAP had already cut its debt by four billion francs through the listing of its Sun Life and Provincial Holding unit in London and raised 500 million francs through the sale of German insurance operations. UAP also recently sold some Chilean operations.
Axa recently announced completion of the disposal of its 9.7 percent stake in Scor while AGF is only keeping a token holding of 0.7 percent after having sold nine percent.

Scor's shares, which closed at 199.0 francs on Monday, have fallen back from their year high of 224.40 francs hit in July amid fading speculation the recent wave of acquisition activity in the reinsurance sector could make it a takeover target.
